In the 2026/27 tax year, which runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027, adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs.

You can split that between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance does not carry forward.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The ISA allowance for 2026/27 is £20,000 for adults aged 18 or over. The tax year runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027. You can split the allowance between cash, stocks and shares, and innovative finance ISAs, and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance does not carry forward.

The cash ISA cap for under-65s starts from 6 April 2027, so it doesn't apply in 2026/27.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

I couldn't find anything that says whether a 17-year-old can open an ISA with us. The ISA guide only covers adults aged 18 or over, who can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs in the 2026/27 tax year. It also says a Lifetime ISA can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39, so she is too young for that one.

For a definite answer about your daughter's options, please ask an adviser or call the switchboard.

You can pay up to £4,000 a year into a Lifetime ISA. That counts towards the £20,000 overall ISA allowance. The government adds a 25% bonus, up to £1,000 a year.

You can open one if you're aged 18 to 39. Withdrawals for other reasons than those below incur a 25% government charge. Withdrawals are free of charge for a first home costing £450,000 or less (the account must have been open at least 12 months), from age 60, or if you are terminally ill with less than 12 months to live.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

At 42, you're too old to open a Lifetime ISA. According to our ISA guide, they can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39.

You can still pay up to £20,000 a year into other types of ISA if you're 18 or over. For advice on which one suits you, I can pass you to an adviser. Details are in our ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The changes take effect from 6 April 2027:

- Investors under 65 can pay at most £12,000 into cash ISAs each tax year. The overall £20,000 ISA allowance is unchanged, so the rest can go into stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.
- Transfers from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs will no longer be permitted.
- A charge will apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares or innovative finance ISA.
- Money already in cash ISAs isn't affected by the cap.

This is general information, not personal advice. Your adviser can discuss what it means for you. More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

According to our ISA guide, the new cap doesn't apply to you at 70. From 6 April 2027, the cash ISA limit will be £12,000 a year for investors under 65. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.

The guide also says money already in cash ISAs isn't affected by the cap. Transfers from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs will no longer be permitted from that date. I can't advise on what you should do with your own money. Please raise that with your adviser.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Under HM Revenue & Customs' guidelines, ISA transfers should complete within 30 calendar days. Transfers between cash ISAs should take no more than 15 working days. Re-registering holdings in specie can take longer if fund managers are slow to respond.

If the holdings are sold first and moved as cash, the proceeds move once the sales have settled. That is normally within four working days of dealing.

The new provider starts the transfer, and we don't charge for transfers in or out. We update you through the portal at each stage.

More detail: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

Yes. Our stocks and shares ISA is flexible. Money you withdraw during a tax year can be replaced in the same tax year without using more of your allowance.

The documents don't say whether the same applies to ISAs you hold elsewhere. More detail is in our ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Yes, in part. A surviving spouse or civil partner gets an additional permitted subscription equal to the value of the deceased's ISAs. This is on top of their own allowance. It applies whether or not they inherit the investments themselves.

Also, the ISA stays tax-free as a continuing account of a deceased investor for up to three years while the estate is administered. ISAs still form part of your estate for inheritance tax.

The guide is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/ If you'd like to talk about your own circumstances, I can pass you to a person.

The pension annual allowance is £60,000. If the total paid into your pensions in a tax year goes over it, an annual allowance charge is normally due. That total includes employer contributions and the value of any defined benefit accrual.

- **Tapering:** For high earners, the allowance tapers down to a minimum of £10,000.
- **Carry forward:** You can carry forward unused allowance from the previous three tax years. You must have been a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.
- **Money purchase annual allowance:** If you have taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, a £10,000 money purchase annual allowance applies to further defined contribution contributions.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

I can't advise on how this applies to you. For that, please raise it with your adviser.

Yes, you can still pay into it, but the money purchase annual allowance applies. Once you've taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, the money purchase annual allowance of £10,000 applies to further defined contribution contributions.

The information I have doesn't say how this applies to your own circumstances. Please raise that with your adviser. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

claims: The answer says 'a lower limit applies'. The evidence states only that the £10,000 money purchase annual allowance applies. It does not compare this to any other limit, so 'lower' is an added comparative claim.

Normally, you can take up to 25% of a pension tax free. This is subject to the lump sum allowance of £268,275 across all your pensions. Lump sums above the allowance are taxed at your marginal rate.

I can't say how much you should take or when. If you want advice on that, I can pass your question to an adviser. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

You can draw from a defined contribution pension from age 55. This rises to 57 from 6 April 2028. The options are flexi-access drawdown, buying an annuity, taking lump sums, or a combination. Each has different tax consequences.

When you apply to access a pension, we will refer you to Pension Wise. We will also offer to book a free guidance appointment for you, unless you have already had one or have received regulated advice.

More detail is on the Pensions page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

I can't advise on which option suits you. If you'd like that, I can pass you to an adviser.

Yes. If the transfer value is more than £30,000, the law requires you to take appropriate independent advice before the transfer can proceed. The advice must come from a firm with Financial Conduct Authority permission to advise on pension transfers. Fernhill Wealth holds that permission.

The Financial Conduct Authority expects advisers to start from the assumption that a transfer won't be suitable. Fernhill recommends one only where it can show the transfer is clearly in your interest. The documents don't cover transfers below £30,000, so please raise that with an adviser.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

From 6 April 2027, most unused pension funds and death benefits will be included in the value of your estate for inheritance tax. Benefits passing to a spouse or civil partner, or to a registered charity, remain exempt. Dependants' scheme pensions and death-in-service benefits are outside the new rules.

Income tax is separate. If you die before 75, benefits are normally paid free of income tax, within the lump sum and death benefit allowance of £1,073,100. If you die at or after 75, the recipient pays income tax at their marginal rate.

I can't say how this applies to your own circumstances. For that, please speak to an adviser. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes, you can. Your own contributions get tax relief up to 100% of your relevant UK earnings in the tax year, or £3,600 gross if your earnings are lower. With no earnings, the £3,600 gross figure is the limit that applies.

Basic-rate relief is added to the pension automatically. Our guide is here: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

I can't tell you whether you should contribute or how much. If you want advice on that, I can pass you to an adviser.

Yes. Our pensions guide says unused annual allowance from the previous three tax years can be carried forward. You must have been a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.

The guide gives the annual allowance as £60,000. For high earners it tapers down to a minimum of £10,000. The guide doesn't say how much you personally could carry forward. Please raise that with your adviser.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

A full financial plan costs £2,400, plus VAT where it applies. It covers a review of your whole financial position, a written plan with recommendations, and a meeting to go through it.

One-off advice on a single topic costs £1,200, plus VAT where it applies. Financial planning is available at any level of wealth.

More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

Ongoing advice costs 0.75% a year of the assets under advice. It's collected monthly from your accounts.

It covers your annual review meeting, access to your adviser throughout the year, rebalancing recommendations and the quarterly reports.

More detail is on the fees and charges page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/
